clue.text: A Greek hotel, one on a mountain

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the hotel and one after the mountain

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain, as in the Swiss Alps
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A stands for one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A Greek innkeeper running a lodge high up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to our A, so it is 'A Greek' letter.

clue.text: Somewhere in US, a science establishment attended by a graduate

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is where science is done
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree holder

explanation.surface: A US research lab gets a new graduate on its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a southern state of the USA, so it is a place somewhere in the country.

clue.text: Hike in cost of hash? Maybe grow your own…..

definitions.meaning: hash is cannabis, also called pot, so a rise in its price is the pot going up
gardeners move seedlings into bigger containers, which is what you would do growing your own plants

explanation.surface: Faced with dearer cannabis, a smoker decides to cultivate their own plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it is the price of pot rising; as a gardening verb it means moving a plant into a pot.

clue.text: …drug, hopin' to get high?

indicators.note: the apostrophe in this clipped word shows the final G is dropped, as in speech

parts.note: aspiring is reaching upwards, wanting to rise

explanation.surface: A druggie hoping a pill will give them a high.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's cannabis theme. 'Hopin'' drops its G the way ASPIRING must.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common painkilling medicine, an everyday example of a drug.

clue.text: Son who when abroad is detained by regimes causes concern

indicators.note: the son and the French word are held within the regimes, like prisoners

parts.note: diets are regimes of eating
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A son travelling abroad is held by foreign governments, worrying his family.
explanation.definitionFit: To disquiet is to make uneasy, so it means causing worry or anxiety.

clue.text: Gives info why not to shop in Norfolk town on Tue PM say?

indicators.note: signals the phrase is spoken, so the two words run together

parts.words: why not to shop in Norfolk town on Tue PM
parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk; shops in many small British towns closed on one afternoon a week, so the reason is that Diss closes

explanation.surface: Someone explains why shopping in a Norfolk town on a Tuesday afternoon is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, England; British towns traditionally had an early-closing day when shops shut in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal or make known, so it means giving out information.

clue.text: Shoot is cut just above earth

indicators.note: in a down clue the cut sits directly above the earth

parts.note: to snip is to cut with scissors
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A gardener trims a plant's shoot right at soil level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a plant shoot, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to fire at someone from a hidden position, a kind of shooting.

clue.text: Fruit that's French is most unappealing

parts.note: ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo
est is French for 'is', the verb in 'that's'

explanation.surface: A greengrocer declares that a French fruit is the least attractive on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unattractive, so the superlative is the most unattractive.

clue.text: Upset? Turn volume up on almost everything about oneself

indicators.note: in a down clue the turned volume sits up on top of the rest
turning the volume round sets the word running the other way

parts.note: a tome is a big book, a volume
I is oneself, the speaker
on is kept as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: all is everything

explanation.surface: Someone turns up the volume on a self-absorbed rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses TOME to EMOT, placed 'up' above the rest; 'almost' trims ON ALL to ONAL, which goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset is overcome by feeling, which is being moved or stirred.

clue.text: Spy's cover blocks ways of proceeding

indicators.note: a cover is the outside, so only the first and last letters of the word are kept

parts.note: to stem is to block or stop a flow

explanation.surface: A spy's false identity obstructs official procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a spy's false identity but takes the outside letters of Spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or set procedure for doing things.

clue.text: Historically negative stance I adopted for starters?

indicators.note: the I is taken on at the end

parts.note: being anti is a stance against something
past refers to history, as opposed to now

explanation.surface: Someone once opposed a position but has since taken it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian hors d'oeuvres served before the main meal are appetisers, the dishes that begin it.

clue.text: Back to college for bad speller according to appearances?

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a poor speller might write school, a college, as it sounds

explanation.surface: A poor speller is sent back to school, judging by how things look.
explanation.walkthrough: SKOOL is a jokey misspelling of school, made famous by the Molesworth books.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's looks are their outward appearance.

clue.text: With very soft lining, a real tight old dress

indicators.note: the very soft letters line the inside of the rearranged words
tight means drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: A snug old-fashioned garment with a very soft lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' scrambles A REAL to AAREL, and PP sits inside it after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a rather old-fashioned word for clothing or attire.

clue.text: Solitary before having a wee one

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a tiny creature or a small child

explanation.surface: A lone person, before company arrives, has a small child with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse lives alone, a solitary figure.

clue.text: They're a flaming nuisance

parts.note: 'flaming' sounds like mild swearing but literally describes people who set fires

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about some annoying people.
explanation.definitionFit: People who start fires deliberately cause blazes, a literally fiery menace.

clue.text: The drink that's very easy to make?

definitions.text: The drink that's very easy to make?

parts.note: the drink is a nickname for the sea
a breeze is something very easy

explanation.surface: Asking which cocktail is simplest to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cocktail of vodka and fruit juices; split up, the words are the ocean and an easy task.

clue.text: Alien turning right to left? Yes in a weird way

indicators.note: right and left are the letters R and L, one switched for the other

parts.note: a stranger is an alien, an outsider

explanation.surface: An alien switches from political right to left, and says yes oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final R of STRANGER becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oddly or peculiarly is acting in an unusual manner.

clue.text: Get to grips with these Chinese gangs

definitions.meaning: a gripping tool with two arms, used to pick things up
secret criminal societies among Chinese communities

explanation.surface: Tackling Chinese organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a two-armed gripping tool; the other is the name for Chinese secret societies.

clue.text: Wrap fruit that's in between small and large

indicators.note: the fruit sits between the two size letters

parts.note: S is the size abbreviation for small
L is the size abbreviation for large
a haw is the berry of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Wrapping a fruit sized somewhere between small and large.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing sizes S and L frame HAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a garment draped around the shoulders, a scarf-like covering.

clue.text: Drink beer? Remember first half is best

parts.note: to sup is to drink, as one sups beer

indicators.note: the first half of the word is kept, its first four letters

explanation.surface: Advice to drink beer, remembering that the first half is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supreme is the highest or finest, the very top.

clue.text: We hope for a drop off in such music

definitions.text: We hope for a drop off in such music

parts.words: We hope for a drop off in such music
parts.note: 'drop off' sounds like a fall in volume but means falling asleep

explanation.surface: Musicians hoping the noise will die down.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing song is sung to send a child to sleep, which is dropping off.

clue.text: Left hand's traces showing carelessness — second pinch produced blood

parts.note: to crib is to pinch, to steal or copy
to bleed is to produce blood

explanation.surface: A left-hander's careless marks, and a second nip draws blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing scrawled hastily leaves messy marks of the hand, done without care.

clue.text: Network's taken over before long to add glamour

indicators.note: the turned network comes before the longing
taken over means turned over, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a web is a network
to long is to itch, to yearn

explanation.surface: A network is bought out before being glammed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamour originally meant a magic spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour once meant a spell, so to enchant is to cast one.

clue.text: Mostly horrible oddly overlooked samples of one doll's dresses

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: dire means horrible or dreadful

indicators.note: the odd letters are passed over, so only the even ones are sampled

explanation.surface: Nasty clothes for a doll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims DIRE to DIR; the even letters of 'one doll's' give NDLS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are full-skirted Alpine peasant frocks, a kind of women's dress.

clue.text: Leopard mistakenly let out

indicators.note: something done mistakenly is done wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A zoo animal released by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners granted early release on conditions are freed, allowed out.

clue.text: Dance band is completely boxed in

indicators.note: the letters are enclosed within these words, boxed inside them

explanation.surface: A dance band is completely hemmed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub party with dancing to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Latter-day hippie Neville's jacket put on a flutter

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside, so only the outer letters of the name are kept

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: Neville stakes his jacket on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of alternative spirituality and lifestyle in recent decades are modern successors of the hippie.

clue.text: About drink that's brought over, he's bought it

indicators.note: brought over means flipped, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
nog is a strong ale or eggnog

explanation.surface: A drink is carried across, and someone has paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has 'bought it' has died, so he is beyond saving.

clue.text: In the end medical procedure partially came near to relapse

indicators.note: to relapse is to fall back, so the letters run backwards
only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: A patient almost recovered but then relapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: This procedure injects fluid into the rectum, at the rear end of the body.

clue.text: Made agreeable little number in special edition

indicators.note: the small number is placed inside the edition letters

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A small number of copies printed in a special edition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten something is to make it more pleasant or acceptable.

clue.text: All extremely juvenile ringing head of department after close of office

indicators.note: the rest follows the closing letter
the close is the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: very means extremely

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the boy goes round the letter

parts.note: a boy is a juvenile

indicators.note: the head is the first letter

explanation.surface: Every very young person called the department head after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like phoning, but puts BOY round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means every person, all of them.

clue.text: Measure of frequency in sound as causes damage

indicators.note: spoken out, the unit name matches another word

parts.note: the hertz is the unit of frequency, cycles per second

explanation.surface: A frequency measurement shows how a sound can do damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt is to injure or harm.
